handbookNote: Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 423, "Notaries Public and Commissioners of Foreign Deeds" (43 active sections: KRS 423.110-.200, the 1970/1972 Uniform Recognition of Acknowledgments Act, plus the core modern notary law at KRS 423.300-.465, Kentucky's 2019/2020 RULONA-style adoption, 2019 Ky. Acts ch. 86). Classification: APPLICATION-ONLY -- KRS 423.390(2) lists commissioning requirements (18+, US citizen/permanent resident, county residency or employment, English literacy, not disqualified under KRS 423.395) with no exam and no mandatory training/education course anywhere in the chapter; KRS 423.415(2) gives the Secretary of State only permissive authority to someday impose training by regulation, not a current statutory mandate. Content depth rationale: unusually well-developed electronic/online-notary regime for a state this size -- separate Secretary of State registration for online notaries (KRS 423.390(10)-(15)), audio-visual journal requirements for online notarial acts (KRS 423.380, 423.355(5)), tamper-evident technology requirements (KRS 423.385), and a full remote-located-individual notarization framework (KRS 423.455) -- which is what makes a genuinely grounded ~130-question bank possible despite the application-only classification. Distinctive quirk documented and tested throughout this track: Kentucky splits the commissioning process between two different offices -- the Secretary of State issues the commission itself (KRS 423.390(1)-(3)), but the notary must then personally appear before the COUNTY CLERK within 30 days to take the oath of office and file a $1,000 surety bond (KRS 423.390(4)-(5)), and may only act while that bond remains on file with the clerk. Pricing: $0.75 (75 cents) -- reflects this project's established tier for application-only states with no graded assessment, consistent with the site owner's 2026-08-14/16 scoping directive for Kentucky notary.
